name: US Chamber of Commerce

summary.text: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce is a business federation that, according to OpenSecrets data, has been the largest federal lobbying spender in most years since 2001. In 1971 the Chamber's education committee chairman Eugene Sydnor commissioned the confidential memorandum by Lewis Powell known as the Powell Memo. In August 2009 the Chamber petitioned the EPA for a public hearing on its proposed greenhouse gas endangerment finding, which a Chamber official compared to 'the Scopes monkey trial of the 21st century'; Apple, Exelon, Pacific Gas & Electric, PNM Resources and PSEG then left the Chamber, and Nike left its board, over its climate position. In 2019 the Chamber published a position stating that the climate is changing, humans are contributing, and 'inaction is not an option', while continuing to oppose regulation of greenhouse gas emissions.

facts.claim: According to OpenSecrets data, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce has been the leading federal lobbying spender since 2001. It reported $43.7 million in 2018 and, per Statista's summary of OpenSecrets figures, $53.4 million in 2024, when it ranked second behind the National Association of Realtors.
facts.quote: The US Chamber of Commerce spent the second most that year, for a total of 53.4 million U.S. dollars.

facts.claim: On 23 August 1971 Lewis F. Powell Jr., two months before his nomination to the Supreme Court, wrote a confidential memorandum titled 'Attack on American Free Enterprise System' for Eugene B. Sydnor Jr., chairman of the Chamber's Education Committee, proposing that business organise to defend itself against critics. The memo became public in September 1972 through columnist Jack Anderson, after which the Chamber printed the full text in its newsletter.
facts.quote: It became public in September 1972, when syndicated columnist Jack Anderson wrote about it, and the Chamber then printed the full text in its newsletter

facts.claim: In August 2009 the Chamber, in a petition prepared by the law firm Kirkland & Ellis, asked the EPA to hold a public hearing on its proposed finding that greenhouse gases endanger public health, or else withdraw the proposal. William Kovacs, the Chamber's senior vice president for environment, technology and regulatory affairs, told the Los Angeles Times the hearing would be 'the Scopes monkey trial of the 21st century'.
facts.quote: William Kovacs, the chamber's senior vice president for environment, technology and regulatory affairs, told the Los Angeles Times this hearing would be "the Scopes monkey trial of the 21st century"

sources.title: Chamber calls for 'Scopes monkey trial' on climate change
Chamber of Commerce: Nixon to China Moment or 'Scopes Monkey Trial'?

facts.claim: In autumn 2009 Apple, Exelon, Pacific Gas & Electric, PNM Resources, PSEG and Levi Strauss left the Chamber, and Nike left its board, over the Chamber's position on climate regulation. Apple's resignation letter to Chamber president Thomas Donohue said the company supports regulating greenhouse gas emissions and found it frustrating that the Chamber was at odds with it.
facts.quote: Apple supports regulating greenhouse gas emissions, and it is frustrating to find the chamber at odds with us in this effort.

facts.claim: In 2019 the Chamber published a climate position stating that the climate is changing, that humans are contributing to those changes, and that inaction is not an option, while proposing market-based and technology-led approaches rather than regulation of greenhouse gas emissions.
facts.quote: Its website has asserted that the climate is changing, humans are contributing to these changes, and inaction is not an option.

sources.title: The Chamber's Climate Position: Inaction Is Not an Option
Chamber changes tune on climate, but Dems remain skeptical

facts.claim: A 2020 report by the campaign group Change the Chamber counted 57 Chamber lobbying efforts related to energy and the environment from 2019 to mid-2020 and said the dozen on which the Chamber succeeded were all pro-fossil-fuel outcomes. The World Resources Institute separately criticised the Chamber's 2019 congressional scorecard for not accounting for climate action.
facts.quote: It said the organization's efforts were successful on a dozen of those items — all of which, the report says, "were pro-fossil fuel outcomes."

sources.title: After Calling for Climate Action, US Chamber of Commerce Pushes Pro-Fossil Fuel Agenda
How the Chamber of Commerce's Scorecard Elevates Climate Deniers

connections.claim: The Chamber, through Education Committee chairman Eugene Sydnor, obtained the August 1971 confidential memorandum from Lewis Powell that proposed a business campaign against critics of free enterprise; the Chamber later published its full text.
connections.quote: The 1971 memo is a confidential document that Lewis F. Powell Jr. wrote for Eugene B. Sydnor Jr., chair of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce's Education Committee.

connections.claim: Exelon left the U.S. Chamber of Commerce in 2009 over the Chamber's opposition to greenhouse gas regulation, one of several companies to do so that autumn.
connections.quote: Apple was the most recent in a string of high-profile defections including Exelon, Pacific Gas & Electric, PNM Resources, Nike, Levi Strauss & Co. and PSEG.

connections.claim: Apple resigned from the U.S. Chamber of Commerce in October 2009, telling Chamber president Thomas Donohue that it supported regulating greenhouse gas emissions and objected to the Chamber's opposition to the EPA's effort.
connections.quote: Apple supports regulating greenhouse gas emissions, and it is frustrating to find the chamber at odds with us in this effort.

sources.title: Apple joins an exodus of companies from US Chamber of Commerce

connections.claim: Shell is a member of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce; in its April 2019 trade association review Shell listed the Chamber among groups with which it had some misalignment on climate policy but said it would engage further rather than leave.
connections.quote: Shell also named nine other groups that it disagreed with, including the American Petroleum Institute and the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, but said it would "engage further" with them.

sources.title: Shell to leave AFPM in 2020 over climate 'misalignment'

openQuestions: OpenSecrets' own pages were not among the results; the lobbying totals are cited through Statista and a trade publication that credit OpenSecrets.
The Chamber's response to the 2009 resignations was not found.
A secondary summary reported the Chamber as the top spender in 2025 at $72.1 million; this was not verified.
The Chamber's current climate position page has been updated since 2019 and should be read as the company's present stance.
